skill.name: motion-design
skill.description: Applies motion design principles to create emotionally-driven, technically sound animations and transitions. Provides timing, easing, choreography, and Disney animation principles adapted for UI. Use when creating animations, transitions, micro-interactions, loading states, page transitions, scroll-triggered effects, or any motion work. Works with CSS, Framer Motion, GSAP, Lottie, Spring, or any animation system.
skill.summary: Plan and review UI animations with guidance on timing, easing, sequencing, and reduced motion.
skill.author: lottiefiles

security_audit.summary: Sixteen matches are false positives: they are motion design guidance or an internal documentation link. The export guide documents optional user-scoped registration of a remote service that can process scene data. No evidence found of prompt injection or unauthorized data transfer.

remediation.issue: The optional Creator MCP setup persists in user settings and enables remote processing of animation scene data.
remediation.suggestion: Explain what scene data leaves the client and where it goes. Ask the user to approve setup and remote submission separately.

content.user_title: Design Clear and Accessible UI Motion
content.value_statement: Inconsistent timing and excessive movement can make interface changes hard to follow. Use motion patterns, timing tables, and reduced-motion guidance to plan and review animations.
actual_capabilities: Recommend durations and easing curves for buttons, dialogs, page transitions, and loading states.
Choose position, scale, rotation, or opacity based on what the interaction needs to communicate.
Define a consistent motion style with a signature easing curve, duration tiers, and an entrance pattern.
Sequence groups of elements with staggered starts and a clear focal element.
Adapt motion for small screens and suggest alternatives for people who prefer reduced motion.
limitations: The skill provides design guidance and does not render animation files on its own.
Rendered exports through Creator MCP require a separate remote connection and sign-in.
Timing tables provide starting points, not guarantees of frame rate or responsiveness.
The accessibility checklist does not replace testing in the implemented interface.

use_cases.title: Plan consistent interaction feedback
use_cases.description: Define how a checkout button responds to a press, a pending request, and a successful payment.

use_cases.title: Review a slow modal transition
use_cases.description: Adjust entrance and exit easing, remove unnecessary movement, and specify a reduced-motion alternative.

use_cases.title: Define a shared motion style
use_cases.description: Choose an easing curve, three duration tiers, and a common entrance pattern for a product design system.

prompt_templates.title: Choose button feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest a subtle press animation for a Save button. Give the property, duration, and easing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a dialog transition
prompt_templates.prompt: Specify the opening and closing motion for a settings dialog. Include timing, easing, and a reduced-motion alternative with no spatial movement.

prompt_templates.title: Review a dashboard reveal
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the order and stagger for a dashboard with one key metric and six supporting cards. Provide separate desktop and mobile sequences. Keep the content usable during the animation.

prompt_templates.title: Define motion rules for a design system
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a restrained motion system for an enterprise app. Define signature easing, three duration tiers, and rules for feedback, navigation, and reduced motion. Map them to buttons, dialogs, and page transitions.

output_examples.input: Suggest a calm opening and closing transition for a settings dialog.
output: Open over 320 milliseconds with ease-out. Fade in while scaling from 98 percent to full size.
Close over 230 milliseconds with ease-in. Reverse the scale and fade.
For reduced motion, remove scaling and use a short fade.

output_examples.input: Sequence the entrance of a key metric and four supporting dashboard cards.
output: Reveal the key metric first with a 250-millisecond ease-out.
Start the cards in reading order, with 50 milliseconds between starts. Use the same easing for each card.
For reduced motion, show the content together without sliding or stagger.

best_practices: Identify what the user should notice or understand before choosing animated properties.
Use ease-out for entrances and ease-in for exits, then test timing on the target device.
Provide a reduced-motion alternative and keep important status information available as text.
anti_patterns: Using the same duration for a button press and a page transition.
Animating every item at once when only one item needs attention.
Making an error shake the only indication that a form submission failed.

faq.question: Which animation libraries can I use?
faq.answer: The guidance applies to CSS, Framer Motion, GSAP, and React Spring. You can request suggestions for the tools in your project.

faq.question: Can I review an existing animation?
faq.answer: Yes. Share the code or describe the current motion to get feedback on timing, easing, and sequencing.

faq.question: Does the skill cover reduced motion?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests alternatives such as short fades instead of slides, static positioning instead of parallax, and pausing autoplay.

faq.question: Can the skill export a GIF or MP4 by itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents an optional handoff to the hosted Creator MCP service for rendered files.

faq.question: Do I need Creator MCP to work on animation code?
faq.answer: No. You can plan, write, or review animation code without connecting that service.

faq.question: Should I use the suggested durations without changes?
faq.answer: Treat the durations as starting points. Adjust them for the element, travel distance, platform, and how often users see the motion.
